content:
maya: heads up — we've been getting reports of dashboard frame drops and chart stalls in prod starting ~09:10 UTC. noticed CPU spikes on clients and multiple re-downloads of the telemetry bundle.

eoin: yep seeing it in session traces, long tasks around 120–300ms while fetching /api/telemetry/config and then re-importing metrics-client. looks like the new sampling flag causes repeated initializations.

ben: can you paste the network pattern? suspect repeated GETs to /static/telemetry/v2.js or something creating parse/exec thrash.

maya: here, captured in one user session:```GET /api/telemetry/config?sid=abc123 200 20ms
GET /static/telemetry/v2.js 200 180ms
GET /static/telemetry/v2.js 200 175ms
GET /api/metrics?range=60s 200 45ms```

olivia: that double download is the killer — looks like we don't memoize the dynamic import when sampling toggles during feature-flag rollout. the canary toggled from 20% -> 60% -> 100% in 30m (deploy-bot log below).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: feature=telemetry-sampling v2 percent=20 -> 60 -> 100 at 09:05,09:20,09:35 UTC

maya: we need a hotfix. either debounce config fetches or ensure metrics-client is loaded once per page. UX hit right now for power users.

eoin: quick patch idea: add a short-lived in-memory lock on window.__telemetry_loading_promise so subsequent inits await same promise. tiny change in metrics-client wrapper. low risk.

ben: agree. also we should change routing: telemetry config currently proxies through /api which adds auth headers and causes extra preflight for some clients. moving config to /internal/telemetry-config (no cookies, same origin) would reduce latency and avoid revalidation on some CDN rules.

olivia: re: routing, we debated proxy vs internal earlier — proxies let us enforce quotas and RBAC. if we move off /api we lose per-org quota checks. maybe keep /api but add caching headers + ETag so clients can short-circuit fetches.

maya: quotas are important but the client should never re-import the whole bundle on a cache miss. prioritize debounce + in-memory lock now, then follow up with ETag caching + CDN TTL change.

eoin: local patch landed to canary branch: added window.__telemetry_loading_promise + guard, and made import() call idempotent. pushing a rollback is also an option if hotfix fails.

olivia: also adding server-side ETag and Cache-Control: public, max-age=60 on /api/telemetry/config. will open a PR for quota checks to read stale cache and validate async when possible.

maya: can we revert the rollout while we validate? the canary jumped fast and correlated with the spike.

deploy-bot: Revert request queued — rollback telemetry-sampling v2 to previous state at 09:55 UTC, initiating.

sre-ops: monitoring dashboards show client CPU 95th went from 120ms -> 420ms for chart renders during the spike; request rate to /static/telemetry/v2.js multiplied by 4. patch or rollback should help quickly.

eoin: rolling the patch to prod now (metrics-client guard). will post new session traces in 10m.

maya: thanks — if patch stabilizes, follow up action items: 1) Add integration test that simulates feature-flag churn and asserts single dynamic import. 2) Improve server caching headers for config. 3) Doc routing tradeoffs for telemetry (quota vs perf). 4) Add quota-aware read-through cache on the proxy.

ben: +1. also add a telemetry metric: dynamic-imports-per-session so we detect regressions early.

olivia: PRs: server cache header change (WIP), metrics-client guard (merged to canary -> promoting). will ping once staging looks good.

eoin: quick snapshot after patch: dynamic-imports-per-session down from 3.8 -> 1.0 in sampled sessions, client render p99 dropped ~180ms.

maya: closing for now — keep an eye on rollout velocity and add the integration test before next flag flip. :thumbsup:

ben: thx all.

sre-ops: alert silence requested until 12:30 UTC to avoid noise while we validate fix.
